previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted for acute respiratory distress and found to have Pseudomonas pneumonia and recurrent C. difficile colitis. He was treated with IV cefepime for pneumonia and oral vancomycin for C. diff, with a PICC line placed for antibiotic administration. His respiratory status improved to baseline on 35% oxygen, and he remained afebrile with stable labs. Chronic issues including right leg pain, seizure disorder, and psychiatric conditions were managed with home medications. He was discharged to extended care with plans to complete a 14-day course of IV antibiotics and an additional two weeks of oral vancomycin, with follow-up coordinated through his care team.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old male with past medical history of AIDS complicated 
by multiple infections and resulting aphasia, chronic 
respiratory failure requiring trach/PEG, recurrent  c.diff, 
admitted ___ for respiratory failure ___ pseudomonas PNA 
presenting from ___ ICU for respiratory distress and

recurrent PNA. 

# Pneumonia: Difficult to discern on CXR from underlying chronic 
interstitial changes. Concern for infection based on history of 
pseudomonal infection and OSH SIRS criteria including 
hypotension, tachycardia. Patient continuing to endorse frequent 
sputum, ultimately with pseudomonas and klebsiella both seen. 
Initially on vanc/zosyn, later changed to zosyn alone based on 
sensitivities. Plan for 2 week course finishing ___. 
Continued to have significant secretions but vital signs stable 
and appeared well at time of discharge. 

# History of C. diff - patient seen by ID who recommended 
empiric PO vanc 125 mg q6h until 7 days after finishing IV abx. 
Later developed loose stools that decreased in frequency. C. 
diff ordered but not sent.

# HIV status: pt has hx of HIV, last VL 24, CD4 182 in 
___. Hx of poor compliance on ART. CD4 rechecked at 106, 
viral load 101 copies/ml.
-Continued home ___ 1 tab daily, Darunavir  
800 mg PO DAILY, RiTONAvir 100 mg PO daily.  
-Continued home atovaquone and azithromycin prophylaxis.
-Outpatient ID appointment f/u scheduled for further 
monitoring/adjustment of regimen

# ? UTI vs. colonization: dirty UA on presentation. Found to 
have intermediate range vre growing, likely colonization rather 
than UTI. Foley later d/c'd with patient voiding independently 
however with regular incontinence.

# Positive blood cultures, likel contaminant: blood cultures 
obtained on admission returned ___ showing GPCs in clusters, 
coag negative. Most likely consistant with staph epidermidis 
contamination of culture. Repeat cultures were negative. Patient 
has trach and ___, though no obvious sign of skin or soft 
tissue infection. No obvious joint swelling or tenderness. No hx 
cardiac devices. Difficult cardiac exam ___ roncherous breath 
sounds, though no evidence of endocarditis. CXR obtained shows 
diffuse interstitial changes, though no obvious exam or imaging 
findings to suggest septic emboli. No CVA tenderness to suggest 
splenic abscess.  

# Ortho:
Patient with known bilateral hip AVN based on last ortho note, 
was supposed to f/u with ortho but appt not ketp. Ordered plain

contractions, and continue to wear his brace if at all possible.
